newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says Zaire peace talks to start Saturday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says Zaire peace talks to start Saturday.

text.p: South Africa announced on Friday that peace talks would go ahead in Pretoria on Saturday between representatives of the Zairean government and rebels who have overrun the east of the country.
The talks had appeared in doubt following political confusion in Zaire's capital Kinshasa and reports of continued advances by the rebels in the mining regions of central Zaire.

South Africa's Foreign Affairs Ministry said in a brief press statement that talks would start at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Saturday at the government's main headquarters, the Union Buildings, in Pretoria.

The announcement coincided with reports that the rebel forces of Laurent Kabila, who is demanding that President Mobutu Sese Seko step down, had entered the diamond mining capital of Mbuji-Mayi on Friday after government troops fled.

In South Africa Kabila's negotiators said Mobutu's team did not appear to be serious about talks and indicated they would leave if discussions did not begin without delay. A Zairean government official said: "There are procedures we must follow. They cannot expect us to jump on things."
